new.title: Admire the black lava cathedral of Clermont
new.desc: Notre-Dame-de-l'Assomption was begun in 1248 under Bishop Hugues de La Tour and is built of dark Volvic lava stone. The Gothic spires rise over the old town and the interior holds large stained-glass windows.
new.tip: Climb the north tower when it is open for the view over the Chaîne des Puys. The Place de la Victoire in front of it has cafés.
new.q: Cathédrale Notre-Dame-de-l'Assomption, Place de la Victoire, Clermont-Ferrand

new.title: Step inside Romanesque Notre-Dame-du-Port
new.desc: One of the five great Romanesque churches of Auvergne, in the old Port quarter, with a pyramidal apse and carved capitals. It is part of the UNESCO Routes of Santiago de Compostela in France listing (1998).
new.tip: Go down to the crypt with its Black Virgin. Combine it with the cathedral in one walk through the old town.
new.q: Basilique Notre-Dame-du-Port, Rue du Port, Clermont-Ferrand

new.title: Cross Place de Jaude and Vercingétorix's statue
new.desc: Clermont's large pedestrian square covers about 35,000 square metres. At its northern end stands Bartholdi's equestrian bronze of Vercingétorix, inaugurated in 1903.
new.tip: Come on the first or third Sunday morning when a producers' market is held here. The tram stops right at the square.

new.title: Walk the Renaissance streets of Montferrand
new.desc: Montferrand was a separate walled town until 1630 and keeps many listed houses, such as the Maison de l'Apothicaire and the Maison de l'Éléphant on rue Kléber. The streets show the late medieval and Renaissance merchant architecture of Auvergne.
new.tip: Start at Place de la Rodade and follow rue Kléber. Ask the tourist office for the Montferrand walking leaflet.
new.q: Maison dite de l'Apothicaire, 2 Rue de la Rodade, Montferrand, Clermont-Ferrand

new.title: Visit L'Aventure Michelin museum
new.desc: The museum on the Michelin site traces the Clermont tyre maker from its beginnings to the Michelin Guide and Bibendum, the tyre mascot. It stands at 32 rue du Clos Four, in the factory district of the city.
new.tip: Check opening days on the official site before going, as the museum is closed on some days and for an annual break. Allow about two hours.
new.q: L'Aventure Michelin, 32 Rue du Clos Four, Clermont-Ferrand

new.title: Find the Renaissance Fontaine d'Amboise
new.desc: Built in 1515 by Jacques d'Amboise, bishop of Clermont, this is one of the city's main historic fountains. It stands on a small square in the old centre, close to the town hall.
new.tip: The better known Fontaine d'Urbain II is on Place de la Victoire nearby. See both on the same loop.

new.title: Browse the Musée d'art Roger-Quilliot
new.desc: Fine-arts museum installed in a former Ursuline convent in Montferrand, with art from the Middle Ages to the 20th century. Its collection includes sculptures by Camille Claudel.
new.tip: Open Tuesday to Sunday and free for under-18s according to Lonely Planet. It is next to Place Louis-Deteix.
new.q: Musée d'art Roger-Quilliot, Place Louis Deteix, Clermont-Ferrand

new.title: See the fortified church of Saint-Léger in Royat
new.desc: A listed church of the 12th century around which old Royat grew, with a 10th-century crypt and fortified walls. It is listed as a monument historique (Mérimée PA00092332).
new.tip: Check access at the tourist office on avenue Auguste Rouzaud as visitor reports differ. Walk on up to the Parc Thermal afterwards.

new.title: Explore the volcano park Vulcania
new.desc: Vulcania, owned by the Auvergne Region, is a volcano science park with a large underground museum inside a cone designed by architect Hans Hollein. It stands in the Chaîne des Puys UNESCO area, about 15 km from Clermont.
new.tip: Open roughly from late March to early November; check the official site for dates. Pair it with the Lemptégy volcano next door.

new.title: Walk inside the Lemptégy volcano
new.desc: A breached scoria cone that was quarried for pozzolana, so its inside can be walked, with the layers of the eruption exposed. Visits on foot, by audio guide or small train take about two and a half hours.
new.tip: The 2026 season opened on 10 February. Book ahead for the train and bring a jacket for the cold crater.

new.title: Tour Château de Murol and its knight shows
new.desc: A large medieval castle on a basalt hill above the village of Murol, with live horseback jousts and a medieval falconry show in season. A night show on Guillaume de Murol runs on summer evenings.
new.tip: Buy tickets on murolchateau.com. Plan for the afternoon animations in school holidays.

new.title: Study the painted capitals of Saint-Nectaire church
new.desc: The Romanesque church on Mont Cornadore has 103 historiated capitals in the nave and choir, among them the Passion, the Apocalypse and the life of Saint Nectaire. It has been a listed monument since 1840.
new.tip: The best-known view is of the chevet from the road below. Go early to avoid the coaches.

new.title: Visit the Romanesque basilica of Orcival
new.desc: Notre-Dame d'Orcival, built between about 1146 and 1178, is a pilgrimage basilica with a crypt that holds a 14th-century wooden Virgin and Child. It was named a minor basilica in 1894.
new.tip: Concerts of the Musicales d'Orcival are held in the square in summer. Combine it with a walk on the Plateau des Dômes.
new.q: Basilique Notre-Dame d'Orcival, Place de la Basilique, Orcival

new.title: Stroll through the village of Saint-Saturnin
new.desc: A Petite Cité de Caractère about 15 km south of Clermont with a 12th-century Romanesque church, one of the five major churches of Auvergne, and a 13th-century royal castle. The church holds a 15th-century polychrome pietà.
new.tip: Walk the lanes behind the church to the castle. Stop for a drink on the village square.

new.title: Wander medieval Besse and its belfry gate
new.desc: Besse-et-Saint-Anastaise is a Petite Cité de Caractère of dark volcanic stone. Its belfry gate with a barbican is the only one that survives of three town gates.
new.tip: The village lies just before the Lac Pavin road. Visit in the morning before the summer crowds.

new.title: See the neo-Byzantine thermal baths of Le Mont-Dore
new.desc: The Établissement thermal, built from 1817 to 1823 on the site of Roman baths, is a neo-Byzantine spa building and is partly listed since 1989. Guided tours are offered.
new.tip: Book a guided tour through the Sancy tourist office. It is at 1 place du Panthéon.
new.q: Établissement thermal du Mont-Dore, Place du Panthéon, Le Mont-Dore

new.title: Discover Thiers cutlery at the Musée de la Coutellerie
new.desc: The museum at 58 rue de la Coutellerie shows six centuries of knife making in Thiers and has cutlers demonstrating the craft. It opened in 1982.
new.tip: The combined ticket with the Vallée des Rouets is cheaper. Check the season, as the museum has short opening days in winter.
new.q: Musée de la Coutellerie, 58 Rue de la Coutellerie, Thiers

new.title: Look for the zodiac apse of Issoire's abbey church
new.desc: Saint-Austremoine, built around 1130 to 1150, is described as the largest Romanesque church in Auvergne. The chevet carries zodiac sculptures and the interior was repainted in the 19th century.
new.tip: Walk round the apse first, then go in. The old town is compact and easy on foot.
new.q: Abbatiale Saint-Austremoine, Place de la République, Issoire

new.title: See Riom's Sainte-Chapelle and clock tower
new.desc: Riom's old centre has the Sainte-Chapelle of 1395 to 1403, the only surviving part of the palace of Jean de Berry, and the Renaissance Tour de l'Horloge with 128 steps. The tower is on rue de l'Horloge.
new.tip: Sainte-Chapelle visits are guided and limited, so ask at the tourist office. Climb the clock tower for the view.
new.q: Sainte-Chapelle, Rue de l'Hôtel de Ville, Riom

new.title: Drink from the springs in Vichy's Hall des Sources
new.desc: The Hall des Sources houses the pump rooms of the Célestins, Lucas, Hôpital, Chomel and Grande Grille springs. A covered iron gallery of about 700 m by Émile Robert wraps around the Parc des Sources.
new.tip: Entry is free. Bring a cup to taste the warm Grande Grille water.
new.q: Hall des Sources, Parc des Sources, Vichy

new.title: Tour the Art Nouveau Opéra de Vichy
new.desc: The opera hall at the Grand Casino opened in 1903 beside the casino built for Napoléon III in 1864-65. It is described as a unique Art Nouveau hall in France.
new.tip: Visits are only on set dates, so check the Vichy tourist office. A show is the other way in.
new.q: Opéra de Vichy, 5 Rue du Casino, Vichy

new.title: Marvel at stage costumes at the CNCS in Moulins
new.desc: The Centre national du costume de scène, in the former Quartier Villars cavalry barracks, holds more than 10,000 costumes from the Paris Opera, Comédie-Française and BnF. It opened in July 2006 and added a scenography space, La Scène, in 2023.
new.tip: Check the current exhibition on cncs.fr before going. It is on the Route de Montilly.
new.q: Centre national du costume et de la scène, Quartier Villars, Route de Montilly, Moulins

new.title: Visit Souvigny priory, home of two Cluny saints
new.desc: The Cluniac priory church holds the relics of abbots Mayeul and Odilon of Cluny and has a double transept. Founded after a 915 gift to Cluny, it is described as the last church in France with such a plan.
new.tip: The saints' tombs, broken in the Revolution, were reassembled in 2008. Look for the Romanesque capitals in the nave.

new.title: Stroll the dark lava streets of Salers
new.desc: Salers is a Plus Beau Village de France, perched at about 950 m, with Renaissance houses in dark volcanic stone and lauze roofs around the Place Tyssandier d'Escous. The Salers cattle breed was recognised in 1852 thanks to Tyssandier d'Escous.
new.tip: Park outside the walls and walk in. Spring and autumn are quieter than August.

new.title: Climb to the summit of Puy Mary
new.desc: From the Pas de Peyrol car park a steep paved path leads in about 1h20 return to the summit at about 1,783 m, in the heart of the Cantal volcano. The views look over radiating glacial valleys.
new.tip: Go early or take the Col de Serre route if the Pas de Peyrol is crowded. Carry water, there is none on the path.
new.q: Puy Mary, Pas de Peyrol, Mandailles-Saint-Julien

new.title: Explore Saint-Flour's upper town and Saint-Pierre cathedral
new.desc: The ville haute sits on a basalt cliff above the Ander valley. The 15th-century cathedral, consecrated in 1466, looks like a fortress and holds the Christ noir; the Musée de la Haute-Auvergne is in the former bishop's palace.
new.tip: Start on Place d'Armes. The museum and cathedral are side by side.

new.title: See Eiffel's Garabit viaduct
new.desc: This iron railway arch over the Truyère is about 565 m long and 122 m above the valley. It was built by Eiffel's firm between 1880 and 1884 and listed as a monument historique in 2017.
new.tip: Viewpoints are free at the A75 rest area and along the road to the lake shore.

new.title: Tour the 15th-century Château d'Anjony
new.desc: The fortified castle at Tournemire is visited only with a guide, for about an hour, and is part of the Route historique des châteaux d'Auvergne. Tournemire itself is a Plus Beau Village de France.
new.tip: Visits are seasonal and the castle is shut on Tuesdays in some periods. Check anjony.fr before going.

new.title: Eat truffade at Le Comptoir
new.desc: Le Comptoir at 42 rue de l'Ange is a busy bistro near the cathedral that serves the potato and cheese dish truffade with Salers beef. Mains cost about 18 to 40 euros.
new.tip: Book ahead, because it is busy at dinner. Try the Salers beef with the truffade.
new.q: Le Comptoir, 42 Rue de l'Ange, Clermont-Ferrand

new.title: Dine at Michelin-starred Apicius
new.desc: Apicius holds one Michelin star and sits upstairs by the Halles Saint-Pierre at 8 place Saint-Pierre. Chef Arkadiusz Zuchmanski cooks modern French dishes.
new.tip: Reserve well ahead. The set lunch menu is the cheaper way in.
new.q: Apicius, Place du Marché Saint-Pierre, Clermont-Ferrand

new.title: Buy ripened Auvergne cheeses at La Ronde des Fromages
new.desc: This cheese ripener has a stand in the Halle Saint-Pierre, the covered market that is open Monday to Saturday. Auvergne AOP cheeses such as Saint-Nectaire are the local choice.
new.tip: Ask for a tasting plate. Hall hours are given as 7am to 7pm Monday to Saturday.
new.q: La Ronde des Fromages, Halle Saint-Pierre, Place Saint-Pierre, Clermont-Ferrand

new.title: Order truffade at Brasserie Le Dôme
new.desc: Brasserie Le Dôme is on the third floor of the Centre Jaude, facing the cinema. The menu is traditional Auvergne cooking with truffade, aligot and Saint-Nectaire.
new.tip: Lunch costs about 15 to 25 euros. Hours differ by listing, so check before going.
new.q: Brasserie Le Dôme, Centre Jaude 3rd floor, 18 Rue d'Allagnat, Clermont-Ferrand

new.title: Taste a Praluline at Pralus Clermont
new.desc: The chocolate maker Pralus runs a shop at 11 rue Blatin where its Praluline brioche, filled with pink praline, is baked daily in the lab. Pralus makes chocolate from the bean.
new.tip: Buy a Praluline warm in the morning. The shop is a few steps from Place de Jaude.

new.title: Try Auvergne chocolates at La Ruche Trianon
new.desc: La Ruche Trianon is a Belle Époque-style chocolate shop in the old town, a family firm over a century old. Its boxes include Pascalines with local bilberry.
new.tip: Ask for the Auvergne assortment as a gift. Check the opening times locally.

new.title: Taste Moinet's Vichy pastilles
new.desc: Confiserie Moinet, a family firm dating from 1852, has made the mint Vichy pastille since 1932 and also makes sucres d'orge and caramels. Its production site is at Bioparc Vichy-Hauterive and it has a shop in Vichy.
new.tip: Look for the Bassin de Vichy or Moinet label, as imitations exist. Buy a tin as a gift.

new.title: Dine at Vichy's Brasserie du Casino
new.desc: This 49-seat brasserie behind the Opéra has a 1920s decor and a wall of photos of artists from the opera house. The chef Olivier Tajetti works with local suppliers.
new.tip: Reserve before an Opéra performance. It is at 4 rue du Casino.
new.q: Brasserie du Casino, 4 Rue du Casino, Vichy

new.title: Taste Fourme d'Ambert at its Maison
new.desc: The Maison de la Fourme d'Ambert et des fromages d'Auvergne is in a 14th-century building at 29 rue des Chazeaux. It shows how the blue cheese is made and offers tastings.
new.tip: Tasting is about 3.50 euros per person on one listing. Guided tours in English exist.
new.q: Maison de la Fourme d'Ambert, 29 Rue des Chazeaux, Ambert

new.title: Taste Saint-Nectaire at the Ferme Roux in Murol
new.desc: The Roux family show how fermier Saint-Nectaire is made and finish with a tasting. Cheese is sold only at the farm, on a route lined with ripening caves.
new.tip: The shop is closed Wednesday afternoons. Check times on the Sancy site.
new.q: GAEC Route des Caves, Ferme Roux, Beaune-le-Froid, Murol

new.title: Watch Saint-Nectaire being made at Ferme Bellonte
new.desc: The Bellonte family have made raw-milk Saint-Nectaire fermier for eight generations. Visits cover milking and cheese making.
new.tip: Milking visits are listed at 15h30 and cheese making at 17h30. Phone ahead.

new.title: Taste Salers cheese in the Cave de Salers
new.desc: The Cave de Salers starts underground in a ripening cellar and has a tasting space and shop for the five Auvergne AOP cheeses. Salers AOP is a raw-milk cheese traditionally made in mountain burons.
new.tip: Ask for Salers Tradition. Buy a wedge for the picnic.

new.title: Eat truffade at Les Templiers in Salers
new.desc: Les Templiers serves local dishes like pounti, truffade, trout and Salers beef, and is praised for hearty portions and fair prices. It is in the old village.
new.tip: Order the truffade with beef. Book for dinner in summer.

new.title: Lunch at the Auberge du Col de Néronne
new.desc: This inn at Saint-Paul-de-Salers lists truffade, Salers beef, Cantal cheese and blueberry tart, with a terrace over the Maronne valley.
new.tip: Sit on the terrace in good weather. Check seasonal opening.
new.q: Auberge du Col de Néronne, 2 Col de Néronne, Saint-Paul-de-Salers

new.title: Dine on Cantal cuisine at Le Cromesquis
new.desc: Le Cromesquis in Aurillac is rated 13/20 by Gault&Millau and cooks refined Cantal-based dishes. Its three set menus cost 38, 46 and 56 euros.
new.tip: Reserve for dinner. Ask for the Cantal beef.

new.title: Eat Auvergne dishes at Chez Geneviève in Saint-Flour
new.desc: This regional bistro at 25-27 rue des Lacs is described by Gault&Millau as a tradition-led spot for locals and also serves as a wine and tapas bar. Menus start at 33.50 euros.
new.tip: Book ahead for dinner. It is in the upper town.
new.q: Chez Geneviève et le Zag, 25-27 Rue des Lacs, Saint-Flour

new.title: Order truffade at Le Bougnat in Le Mont-Dore
new.desc: Le Bougnat is a Mont-Dore restaurant where recent reviews mention truffade, Saint-Nectaire dishes and potée auvergnate.
new.tip: Reserve in the winter season. Check opening dates.

new.title: Buy chocolates at Les Palets d'Or in Moulins
new.desc: Les Palets d'Or at 11 rue de Paris is a Moulins chocolatier of more than a century. France.fr names it a symbol of the city's artisan excellence.
new.tip: Look for the Bourbonnais specialities, then walk to the cathedral.
new.q: Les Palets d'Or, 11 Rue de Paris, Moulins

new.title: Taste local lentils at Folie des Sens in Saint-Flour
new.desc: Folie des Sens at 36 rue de la Rollandie cooks modern, locavore dishes. Michelin notes its use of local produce such as the blond lentil of Saint-Flour.
new.tip: Book ahead. It suits a special dinner after visiting the upper town.
new.q: Folie des Sens, 36 Rue de la Rollandie, Saint-Flour

new.title: Browse the Place de Jaude producers' market
new.desc: A producers' market is held on Place de Jaude on the first and third Sunday of the month, from 7h to 13h according to a city guide. The square also hosts the Christmas market in December.
new.tip: Check dates since a move to the Halles Saint-Pierre has been proposed. Arrive early for local cheese.

new.title: Catch a film at the Clermont short film festival
new.desc: The International Short Film Festival, founded in 1979, runs for about nine days from late January to early February. The 2026 edition was 30 January to 7 February and the 2024 one drew nearly 166,000 admissions.
new.tip: Buy a pass at the start of the week. Check the dates for 2027 on the festival site.
new.q: Maison de la Culture, Boulevard François Mitterrand, Clermont-Ferrand

new.title: Walk up Montjuzet park for the city view
new.desc: A 26-hectare park on a small former volcano at about 486 m with a viewpoint over Clermont, the Limagne and the Chaîne des Puys. It has a table d'orientation and is open daily.
new.tip: Go at sunset. Hours are listed as 7h15 to 21h.

new.title: Stroll the Parc Thermal of Royat
new.desc: Royat's thermal quarter grew around spa buildings of 1852 to 1856 by architect Agis-Léon Ledru, set in a green spa park with the Eugénie drinking fountain. The park is open to visitors.
new.tip: Follow the walking routes from the station. The tourist office is at 1 avenue Auguste Rouzaud.

new.title: Ride the Panoramique des Dômes to the Puy de Dôme
new.desc: An electric rack railway climbs 5.6 km to the summit of the Puy de Dôme, where the remains of the Gallo-Roman Temple of Mercury stand. The ride takes about 15 minutes.
new.tip: Book for summer weekends. Check the operator's site for fares.
new.q: Panoramique des Dômes, Chemin du Couleyras, Orcines

new.title: Hike around the crater of Puy de Pariou
new.desc: From the Goules car park on the D941 near Orcines a trail climbs wooden steps to the rim of the deepest crater of the Chaîne des Puys. Allow about 2h30 return.
new.tip: Start early, as the car park fills in summer.

new.title: Walk the loop around Lac Pavin
new.desc: A 2.7 km easy loop on yellow waymarks circles the volcanic crater lake near Besse in about one hour. Dogs on a leash are allowed.
new.tip: The start is the Parvis du Lac Pavin. Go early, as coaches arrive.

new.title: Swim at the Lac Chambon beaches
new.desc: The Murol and Chambon beaches on this dam lake have Pavillon Bleu status. Pedalos and canoes are for rent, and swimming is supervised in July and August.
new.tip: Swimming is free. Dogs are not allowed on the beach.
new.q: Plage de Murol, Lac Chambon, Murol

new.title: Reach the Puy de Sancy by cable car
new.desc: The Mont-Dore cable car, opened in 1936, goes up in about four minutes, then 864 wooden steps lead to the summit at 1,886 m, the highest point of Auvergne. The stairs are closed to walkers from December to April.
new.tip: A mixed walk and ride takes about 1h30. Check the cable car season.

new.title: Ride up to the Plomb du Cantal from Le Lioran
new.desc: A cable car leaves Le Lioran for the Plomb du Cantal, with about 20 minutes' walk from the upper station to the summit. Walking routes return via the Puy du Rocher.
new.tip: Summer opening hours change by season. Check the Le Lioran site.
new.q: Téléphérique du Plomb du Cantal, Le Lioran, Laveissière

new.title: Hike the glacial Vallée de Chaudefour
new.desc: A national nature reserve of 820 ha created in 1991 near Chambon-sur-Lac, with a 15.5 km loop of 935 m ascent and a gentler valley-floor walk. Dogs are not allowed.
new.tip: The reserve house is open from May to September. Parking is paid in high season.
new.q: Maison de la Réserve naturelle de Chaudefour, Chambon-sur-Lac

new.title: Walk around Lac d'Aydat
new.desc: A 5.5 km waymarked path circles this volcanic dam lake in about 1h30, with a belvedere and pontoons over the wetland. It is open all year and free.
new.tip: Winter walks give views to the Puy de Dôme. The lake lies in the Parc des Volcans d'Auvergne.

new.title: Fly a tandem paraglider from the Puy de Dôme
new.desc: Freedom Parapente, based at Laschamps, runs tandem flights from the summit every day between April and early November. A longer flight, a more sporting one and a steering lesson are offered.
new.tip: Book on the website. Price listings differ, so check before booking.
new.q: Freedom Parapente, 3 Chemin de la Chave, Laschamps, Saint-Genès-Champanelle

new.title: Tour the Vallée des Rouets in Thiers
new.desc: An open-air valley of river-powered knife-grinding mills. The 'Chez Lyonnet' mill is the last still working, and a guided visit lasts about 45 minutes.
new.tip: A combined ticket with the museum was 8 euros in summer 2025. Check opening hours.

new.title: Swim or sail on Lac de Saint-Étienne-Cantalès
new.desc: The reservoir near Aurillac has beaches at Espinet and Rénac, a sailing school and windsurfing. Swimming is supervised in July and August from 14h to 18h45.
new.tip: Swimming is banned outside supervised areas. Check the 2026 leaflet.

new.title: Ride the summer luge at Super-Besse
new.desc: A tyre lift takes you uphill and a 500 m run with seven turns and a short tunnel leads down beside the Lac des Hermines. It is open from age 3 and is not booked in advance.
new.tip: The ticket office is at the Rond-point des Pistes. The Pass Loisirs covers it.
new.q: Luge d'été, Rond-point des Pistes, Super-Besse

new.title: Join the Aurillac street theatre festival
new.desc: The Festival international de théâtre de rue is run by Éclat each August. The 2025 edition was 20 to 23 August and the 2026 edition was listed for 19 to 22 August.
new.tip: Many shows are free. Book beds months ahead.
new.q: Éclat, Centre national des arts de la rue, Aurillac

new.title: Hike the Chouvigny gorge and castle path
new.desc: The Chemin des Murailles climbs to a cross with a view of the Château de Chouvigny, a 13th-century fortress held by the La Fayette family, over the Sioule gorges. A longer 11 km loop leaves from the same village.
new.tip: The trail is slippery after rain. Start from the village by the river.

new.title: Spend the day in Parc Fenestre in La Bourboule
new.desc: This 12 ha park laid out in 1874 beside the Dordogne has playgrounds, a small train, mini golf and slides. A path links it with the Charlannes plateau.
new.tip: Check whether the cable car to Charlannes is running. Good for families.

new.title: Cycle the lac d'Allier loop in Vichy
new.desc: The 6.3 km Boucle du Lac circles the lake formed by the 1963 weir. It joins the Via Allier cycle route, and bikes can be hired at the Vichy station kiosk.
new.tip: Combine it with the 12.7 km Boucle des Isles.

new.title: Soak at the Célestins thermal spa in Vichy
new.desc: The Célestins Spa Thermal is one of Europe's largest spas, built on Vichy mineral water. In 2025 it was described as the only spa in town offering the water while Les Dômes was refurbished.
new.tip: Book treatments in advance. Check the official Vy Resort site.
